title: Customer bridge: streaming deadlock cascade (request amplification) — dial-back hotpatch and mitigation
creator: Sofia Nguyen
description: Summary: A production customer reported sustained 5xx errors and stalled streaming responses during a peak migration. Investigation showed a cascading deadlock triggered by client-side aggressive retries combined with an edge-level streaming multiplexer bug that held connections while backend inference engines experienced KV cache pressure. The effect: amplified request storms, connection exhaustion at the gateway, and tenant-visible tail latency / 502/504s.
actions_taken: Created emergency customer bridge within 30m of escalation and communicated a short-term dial-back guidance to affected customers
Rolled out a staged hotpatch to the gateway to enforce per-connection concurrent-stream limits and early-abort slow multipart streams (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3221)
Deployed an adaptive admission filter that rejects obvious retry-amplified request patterns (idempotency token collisions and identical payload bursts)
Temporarily increased KV cache compaction frequency on the inference pool to reduce memory pressure and unblock hot loops
Applied a coordinated client-side advisory to SDKs: lower retry TTL and enable jittered backoff (SDK issue link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/789)
Added emergency playbook steps to the Runbook: frontdoor fast-fail criteria, tenant soft-quarantine, and telemetry anchors
rollback_plan: If the hotpatch introduces regressions (increased client-side errors or regression in stable tenants), rollback by reverting gateway commit and re-enable pre-hotpatch admission rules. Revert window: 30 minutes with canary verify on us-east-1 and one low-traffic tenant.
comments: 2025-11-15 09:12 - Sofia Nguyen: Pager triggered from CS team — customer A experiencing repeated 502s during large import. Opening bridge.

2025-11-15 09:35 - Daniel Kim: Initial traces show streaming multiplexer holding connection state for >30s under retry storms; backend inference nodes show KV cache thrashing. Correlating with SDK behavior that retries without jitter.
2025-11-15 10:05 - Marco Ruiz (oncall): Scoped mitigation: added early-abort on gateway for streams stalled >10s and limited concurrent streams per TCP connection to 4. Deployed to canary hosts.
2025-11-15 11:20 - QA: Canary looks stable for 45m; error rate for canary tenants decreased from 8% to 0.7%. Proceeding to staged rollout.
2025-11-15 12:00 - Customer Success: Notified customer A of temporary mitigation and recommended SDK update; customer accepted temporary traffic throttling.
2025-11-15 14:40 - Daniel Kim: Hotpatch merged and rolled to all gateways; KV compaction schedule adjusted on inference fleet. Observed normalized p95 for affected tenant.
2025-11-16 08:10 - Observability: Added anchor metrics to dashboards and an alert for retry-amplified payload patterns.

2025-11-18 16:00 - Postmortem note: Root cause: (1) SDK retry semantics incompatible with streaming multiplexer assumptions; (2) rare race in gateway stream state machine leading to connection hold during backend KV eviction; (3) insufficient early-detection of retry storms in admission controller.
2025-11-19 09:30 - Action owner assignments: Daniel -> gateway stream fix (ENG-774446), Priya -> SDK retry changes (ENG-774447), Anya -> admission controller heuristics and telemetry (ENG-774448).
2025-11-20 10:00 - Sofia Nguyen: Customer confirmed resolution; closing incident after 72h monitoring with no recurrence.
next_steps: Complete full gateway state-machine rewrite to remove the race (link: ENG-774446)
Publish SDK stricter retry defaults and automated migration guide (link: ENG-774447)
Enhance admission controller with per-tenant leaky-bucket and anomaly detector for identical payload bursts (link: ENG-774448)
Run chaos tests that simulate client retry storms and KV eviction spikes during CI to prevent regressions
Schedule a post-incident customer debrief with affected tenants and update SLA guidance
